fullPassage:
You are at a critical stage in your life, trying to figure out who you are and who you want to be. You may also be wondering how you can improve yourself. Self-improvement is not about being perfect. It is a journey to become the best version of yourself. The talks here will inspire you as you take your first steps.

Talk 1 For Those Struggling with Creativity
I'm a writer, and I love writing. But there are moments when I feel anxious about my writing and blame myself for a lack of creativity. Creating something new is not easy, and you have probably experienced this when you had difficulty coming up with ideas for group projects or videos. So, how can we set aside those worries and enjoy the creative process more?

I did some research on this issue and found that ancient Romans understood "genius" differently from how we see it today. To them, "genius" didn't refer to a particularly gifted person but rather a divine assistant spirit of creativity. They believed that geniuses lived in the walls of artists' homes and would come out and help them with their work. This meant that if the artists' work was not good enough, they didn't have to blame themselves entirely. Everyone knew that their genius was also responsible for the quality of the work.

Some people may think this is not scientific, but we often hear stories about how people get inspired mysteriously. I once met an American poet named Ruth Stone. Throughout her life, she worked on a farm and wrote poems. She had a special way of recognizing when a poetic genius was coming to her. She said it felt like the earth was shaking under her feet! Whenever that feeling hit her, she knew she had to return home quickly and write the poem down before the genius found another poet.

My creative process isn't as dramatic as hers. I have to get up at the same time and work on my laptop for hours every day. Yet, even in this rather boring routine, I do get ideas coming from a source I can't identify. Typically, it happens when I'm deeply engaged in my work. Several hours or even days can pass, and I completely immerse myself in my creative process. It's at those moments that a brilliant idea strikes me somewhat mysteriously. I'm sure that's my genius.

Remember that you too have a magical genius that is willing to help you. But first, you must put your heart and soul into your work. Immerse yourself in your work and try to enjoy the creative process itself. If you do, your genius will come for sure.

Talk 2 For Those Worrying about an Uncertain Future
When I was 12, I was passionate about soccer. I played soccer every day, and I always thought that I would grow up to become a great soccer player one day. Forty years later, however, I don't even watch soccer games anymore. I'm actually a big fan of American football now. My 12-year-old self may find this a betrayal.

When I was 22, I graduated from college in India with a computer science degree. At that time, it never occurred to me that I would be living a completely different life in the U.S. as a journalist and podcast host. Thirty years ago, we didn't even have podcasts or smartphones, and the future was not just unknown but unknowable.

When we look back, we can see how we have changed, but when we look forward, we tend to imagine ourselves as the same people, only older and taller. That, however, is not the case. Biologically, our cells are continuously renewing themselves, and our brains are rewiring and modifying their connections. We are constantly becoming new versions of ourselves.

Have you heard of the "Ship of Theseus"? When Theseus, a famous Greek hero, returned from his adventure of rescuing the children of Athens, the Athenians wanted to preserve his ship. They kept replacing the wood pieces that had decayed until all the original pieces were replaced with new ones. In this situation, could we still call it the Ship of Theseus?

Well, we are living examples of the Ship of Theseus. Every day, we are changing and growing to become new versions of ourselves. This means that our future selves may be very different from who we are now. Then how can we create a future we'll be proud of? I have some advice for you.

First, actively envision the kind of person you want to become in the future. To do this, spend time with different kinds of people to learn more and stay curious. Second, when expressing your views online or with friends, remember that your future self might disagree with your current opinions. So, be respectful of other people's opinions and don't just assume that you are always right. Finally, your future self will have strengths and wisdom that you may lack today. Even if you can't do something now, you might be able to in the future. So, don't be afraid of new challenges. Be brave!

questions.passage: Creating something new is not easy, and you have probably experienced this when you had difficulty ①<u>coming</u> up with ideas for group projects or videos. I did some research on this issue and found that ancient Romans ②<u>understood</u> "genius" differently from how we see it today. They believed that geniuses ③<u>living</u> in the walls of artists' homes and would come out and help them with their work. This meant that if the artists' work was not good enough, they didn't have to blame ④<u>themselves</u> entirely.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ 'believed that geniuses lived'에서 that절의 동사는 lived(과거형)이 맞다. living(현재분사)으로는 that절이 불완전.
det.analysis:
✅ ① coming: had difficulty + -ing
✅ ② understood: found that + 과거형
❌ ③ living → lived: believed that + 주어 + 동사(과거형). that절에 정형동사 필요
✅ ④ themselves: 재귀대명사. 주어 they = 예술가들이 자신을 탓하다
det.tip: that절에는 정형동사(시제 있는 동사)가 와야 함. believed that they lived (O) vs believed that they living (X).

questions.passage: Whenever that feeling hit her, she knew she had to return home quickly and write the poem down before the genius ①<u>found</u> another poet. My creative process isn't as ②<u>dramatic</u> as hers. Yet, even in this rather boring routine, I do get ideas ③<u>coming</u> from a source I can't identify. It's at those moments ④<u>when</u> a brilliant idea strikes me somewhat mysteriously.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ 'It's at those moments that ...'는 강조 구문이므로 that이 맞다. when은 틀림.
det.analysis:
✅ ① found: before + 과거형
✅ ② dramatic: as + 형용사 + as 비교급
✅ ③ coming: ideas coming from (현재분사 후치수식)
❌ ④ when → that: 'It is ~ that' 강조 구문. It's at those moments that = 바로 그 순간에
det.tip: 강조 구문 'It is ~ that': 시간/장소/이유를 강조할 때도 that을 씀 (when/where 아님). It is at night that I study best.

questions.passage: When Theseus, a famous Greek hero, returned from his adventure of ①<u>rescuing</u> the children of Athens, the Athenians wanted to preserve his ship. They kept ②<u>replacing</u> the wood pieces that had decayed until all the original pieces ③<u>were replaced</u> with new ones. In this situation, could we still call ④<u>them</u> the Ship of Theseus?
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문은 'call it the Ship of Theseus'로, 배 한 척을 가리키므로 it이 맞다. them은 복수.
det.analysis:
✅ ① rescuing: of + -ing (전치사 + 동명사)
✅ ② replacing: kept + -ing
✅ ③ were replaced: 수동태. 나무 조각이 교체당함
❌ ④ them → it: the Ship(단수)을 가리키므로 단수 대명사 it
det.tip: call + 목적어 + 보어: call it the Ship of Theseus. 배 한 척 = it (단수), pieces = them (복수).

questions.passage: You are at a critical stage in your life, trying to figure out who you are and who you want to be. Self-improvement is not about being perfect. It is a journey to become the best version of yourself. But there are moments when I feel ①<u>anxious</u> about my writing and blame myself for a lack of creativity. I did some research on this issue and found that ancient Romans understood "genius" ②<u>differently</u> from how we see it today. She had a ③<u>special</u> way of recognizing when a poetic genius was coming to her. It's at those moments that a brilliant idea strikes me somewhat ④<u>predictably</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문은 '신비롭게(mysteriously)'인데 '예측 가능하게(predictably)'로 바뀌었다. 아이디어가 신비롭게 떠오른다는 맥락.
det.analysis:
✅ ① anxious(불안한): 원문 일치
✅ ② differently(다르게): 원문 일치
✅ ③ special(특별한): 원문 일치
❌ ④ predictably(예측 가능하게) → mysteriously(신비롭게): 반의어 교체
det.tip: mysteriously(신비롭게) ↔ predictably(예측 가능하게). 앞에서 '알 수 없는 원천(source I can't identify)'이라 했으므로 예측 불가.

questions.passage: When we look back, we can see how we have changed, but when we look forward, we tend to imagine ourselves as the same people, only older and taller. Biologically, our cells are continuously ①<u>renewing</u> themselves, and our brains are rewiring and modifying their connections. They kept replacing the wood pieces that had ②<u>decayed</u> until all the original pieces were replaced with new ones. First, actively ③<u>envision</u> the kind of person you want to become in the future. So, be ④<u>dismissive</u> of other people's opinions and don't just assume that you are always right.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문은 '존중하는(respectful)'인데 '무시하는(dismissive)'으로 바뀌었다. 다른 사람의 의견을 존중하라는 조언.
det.analysis:
✅ ① renewing(새롭게 하는): 원문 일치
✅ ② decayed(썩은): 원문 일치
✅ ③ envision(마음속에 그리다): 원문 일치
❌ ④ dismissive(무시하는) → respectful(존중하는): 반의어 교체
det.tip: respectful(존중하는) ↔ dismissive(무시하는). 뒤에 'don't just assume you are always right'와 맥락 일치.

questions.passage: I'm a writer, and I love writing. But there are moments when I feel anxious about my writing and blame myself for a lack of creativity. I did some research on this issue and found that ancient Romans understood "genius" differently from how we see it today. To them, "genius" didn't refer to a particularly gifted person but rather a divine assistant spirit of creativity. This meant that if the artists' work was not good enough, they didn't have to __________.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 작품이 충분하지 않아도 자기 자신을 전적으로 탓하지(blame themselves entirely) 않아도 되었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① blame themselves entirely: 원문 일치
❌ ② 더 나은 작품 만들기: 해당 문맥 없음
❌ ③ 새 genius 찾기: genius는 벽에 살았지 찾는 것이 아님
❌ ④ 직업 포기: 포기 맥락 없음
det.tip: blame oneself entirely = 전적으로 자책하다. 로마인의 genius 개념은 창작 부담을 덜어줌.

questions.passage: When we look back, we can see how we have changed, but when we look forward, we tend to imagine ourselves as the same people, only older and taller. That, however, is not the case. Biologically, our cells are continuously renewing themselves, and our brains are rewiring and modifying their connections. Have you heard of the "Ship of Theseus"? They kept replacing the wood pieces that had decayed until all the original pieces were replaced. The author's main point is that __________.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: we should resist change and stay true to ourselves
biological changes stop once we reach adulthood
we are constantly becoming new versions of ourselves
the Ship of Theseus was never truly preserved

det.korean: 우리는 끊임없이 새로운 버전의 자신이 되고 있다(constantly becoming new versions of ourselves).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ constantly becoming new versions: 원문의 핵심 주장
❌ ① 변화에 저항: 글의 메시지와 정반대
❌ ② 성인이 되면 변화 멈춤: 원문은 계속 변화한다고 함
❌ ④ 배가 보존되지 않았다: 비유일 뿐 주장이 아님
det.tip: 테세우스의 배 비유의 핵심: 모든 부분이 바뀌어도 연속성이 있다 → 우리도 계속 변하지만 여전히 '나'이다.

questions.passage: I'm a writer, and I love writing. But there are moments when I feel anxious about my writing and blame myself for a lack of creativity. I did some research on this issue and found that ancient Romans understood "genius" differently from how we see it today. To them, "genius" didn't refer to a particularly gifted person but rather a divine assistant spirit of creativity.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 고대 로마인들에게 genius는 신성한 보조 영혼이었다.
화자는 창의성에 대해 불안함을 느끼지 않는다.
고대 로마인들은 genius를 재능 있는 사람으로 보았다.

det.korean: ② 원문: 'a divine assistant spirit of creativity' 일치.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 신성한 보조 영혼: 원문 일치
❌ ① 글쓰기를 좋아한다(love writing)
❌ ③ anxious라고 했으므로 불안함을 느낌
❌ ④ gifted person이 아닌 spirit이었음
det.tip: not A but rather B: A가 아니라 오히려 B.

questions.passage: I once met an American poet named Ruth Stone. Throughout her life, she worked on a farm and wrote poems. She had a special way of recognizing when a poetic genius was coming to her. She said it felt like the earth was shaking under her feet! Whenever that feeling hit her, she knew she had to return home quickly and write the poem down before the genius found another poet.
questions.stem: 위 글에서 Ruth Stone에 대한 설명으로 일치하는 것은?
ch: 그녀는 genius가 올 때 천천히 준비했다.
그녀는 genius가 오면 빨리 집으로 돌아가 시를 적었다.

det.korean: ④ 원문: 'she had to return home quickly and write the poem down.' 일치.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 빨리 돌아가 시를 적었다: 원문 일치
❌ ① 도시가 아닌 농장(farm)
❌ ② 인위적이 아닌 자연스러운 방식
❌ ③ quickly(빨리)이지 천천히가 아님
det.tip: 사실 관계: farm에서 일함, 특별한 인식 방법, 빨리 돌아가야 했음.

questions.passage: When I was 12, I was passionate about soccer. Forty years later, however, I don't even watch soccer games anymore. When I was 22, I graduated from college in India with a computer science degree. At that time, it never occurred to me that I would be living a completely different life in the U.S. as a journalist and podcast host. Thirty years ago, we didn't even have podcasts or smartphones.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: ③ 원문: 'graduated from college in India with a computer science degree.' 컴퓨터 공학이지 저널리즘이 아님.
det.analysis:
✅ ① passionate about soccer: 원문 일치
✅ ② big fan of American football now: 원문 일치 (fullPassage 참조)
❌ ③ 인도에서 컴퓨터 공학 전공, 저널리즘은 나중에 미국에서
✅ ④ 팟캐스트 없었음: 원문 일치
det.tip: Computer science degree(컴퓨터 공학 학위) ≠ journalism(저널리즘). 전공과 직업이 다른 것이 이 글의 핵심.

questions.passage: Remember that you too have a magical genius that is willing to help you. But first, you must put your heart and soul into your work. Immerse yourself in your work and try to enjoy the creative process itself. If you do, your genius will come for sure.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 일에 몰입하고 과정을 즐기면 창의적 영감이 찾아온다.
다른 사람의 도움 없이는 창의성을 발휘할 수 없다.

det.korean: 핵심: 일에 몰입하고 과정을 즐기면 genius(영감)가 온다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 몰입+과정 즐기기→영감: 원문 핵심
❌ ① 타고난 재능만: 누구에게나 genius가 있다고 함
❌ ③ 다른 사람의 도움: genius는 추상적 개념
❌ ④ 지루한 일상에서도 아이디어를 얻는다고 함
det.tip: Talk 1의 결론: '심혈을 기울이고 몰입하면 genius가 반드시 온다.'

questions.passage: When we look back, we can see how we have changed, but when we look forward, we tend to imagine ourselves as the same people. That, however, is not the case. We are constantly becoming new versions of ourselves. This means that our future selves may be very different from who we are now. So, don't be afraid of new challenges. Be brave!
questions.stem: 위 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 우리는 끊임없이 변화하므로 새로운 도전을 두려워하지 말아야 한다.
과거의 경험만이 미래를 예측하는 유일한 방법이다.
미래의 자신을 현재와 동일하게 유지해야 한다.

det.korean: Talk 2의 요지: 우리는 끊임없이 변화하므로 새로운 도전을 두려워하지 말라.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 변화+도전: 원문의 핵심 메시지
❌ ② 미래 예측: 미래는 unknowable이라고 함
❌ ③ 변하지 않는다: 원문 정반대
❌ ④ 동일하게 유지: 원문 정반대
det.tip: 'Be brave!' = 용감해져라. 미래 자신에게는 지금 없는 강점과 지혜가 있을 것.

questions.passage: When I was 12, I was passionate about soccer. Forty years later, however, I don't even watch soccer games anymore. I'm actually a big fan of American football now. My 12-year-old self may find this a <u>betrayal</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>betrayal</u>이 이 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 어린 시절의 자신이 예상하지 못한 극적인 변화
인도에서 미국으로 이민 간 것에 대한 후회

det.korean: betrayal(배신)은 12살의 자신이 보기에 40년 후 축구를 버린 것이 배신처럼 느껴질 만큼 극적으로 변했다는 비유.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 어린 시절이 예상 못 한 극적 변화: 자신의 변화를 '배신'으로 비유
❌ ① 친구 배신: 다른 사람이 아닌 자기 자신의 과거
❌ ③ 미식축구 열등: 스포츠 비교가 아님
❌ ④ 이민 후회: 이민 이야기는 별개 맥락(22살)
det.tip: betrayal은 '배신'이지만 여기서는 유머러스한 비유: 12살의 나에게 이건 배신처럼 보일 것이다 = 그만큼 많이 변했다.

questions.passage: To them, "genius" didn't refer to a particularly gifted person but rather a divine assistant spirit of creativity. They believed that geniuses lived in the walls of artists' homes and would come out and help them with their work. This meant that if the artists' work was not good enough, they didn't have to blame themselves entirely. Everyone knew that <u>their</u> genius was also responsible for the quality of the work. Some people may think this is not scientific, but we often hear stories about how people get inspired mysteriously.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>their</u>가 가리키는 대상으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: their genius = 예술가들의 genius. 작품의 질에 대해 genius도 책임이 있었다는 맥락에서 their는 artists를 가리킴.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ the artists: 문맥상 '그들(예술가)의 genius'
❌ ① 로마인 전체: 구체적 맥락에서 예술가에 한정
❌ ② geniuses: genius가 자신의 genius를 가리키면 재귀적 모순
❌ ④ everyone: 주어가 아닌 관찰자
det.tip: 대명사 their의 선행사를 찾을 때 문맥을 확인: 'the artists' work → they = the artists → their genius = the artists' genius.

questions.passage: We are constantly becoming new versions of ourselves. Have you heard of the "Ship of Theseus"? When Theseus, a famous Greek hero, returned from his adventure of rescuing the children of Athens, the Athenians wanted to preserve his ship. They kept replacing the wood pieces that had decayed until all the original pieces were replaced with new ones. In this situation, could we still call <u>it</u> the Ship of Theseus?
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>it</u>이 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: it = 모든 원래 조각이 새 것으로 교체된 배. 'could we still call it the Ship of Theseus?'에서 it은 교체 완료된 배.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 모든 조각 교체된 배: 'In this situation'이 교체 완료 상황을 가리킴
❌ ② 원래 배: 이미 모든 조각이 교체되었으므로
❌ ③ 모험: 문맥상 배를 가리킴

questions.passage: My creative process isn't as dramatic as hers. I have to get up at the same time and work on my laptop for hours every day. Yet, even in this rather boring routine, I do get ideas coming from a source I can't identify. Typically, it happens when I'm deeply engaged in my work.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.
"화자는 일에 깊이 (          ) 할 때 아이디어를 얻는다."

det.korean: 화자는 일에 깊이 몰두(engaged)할 때 아이디어를 얻는다.
det.analysis: 원문: 'deeply engaged in my work.' 빈칸은 engaged.
det.tip: deeply engaged in = ~에 깊이 몰두한. engage in = ~에 참여하다/몰두하다.

questions.passage: When we look back, we can see how we have changed, but when we look forward, we tend to imagine ourselves as the same people, only older and taller. Biologically, our cells are continuously renewing themselves, and our brains are rewiring and modifying their connections.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.
"생물학적으로 뇌는 연결을 재배선하고 (          )하고 있다."

det.korean: 뇌는 연결을 재배선하고 수정(modifying)하고 있다.
det.analysis: 원문: 'rewiring and modifying their connections.' 빈칸은 modifying.
det.tip: modify = 수정하다, 변경하다. rewire = 재배선하다. 둘 다 뇌의 변화를 설명.

questions.passage: First, actively envision the kind of person you want to become in the future. To do this, __________. Second, when expressing your views online or with friends, remember that your future self might disagree with your current opinions.
questions.stem:
주어진 단어를 모두 사용하여 빈칸에 들어갈 문장을 완성하시오. (대소문자 구분 없음, 마침표 생략 가능)
[ spend / time / with / different / kinds / of / people / to / learn / more / and / stay / curious ]
questions.wa: spend time with different kinds of people to learn more and stay curious
accept: spend time with different kinds of people to learn more and stay curious
Spend time with different kinds of people to learn more and stay curious
spend time with different kinds of people to learn more and stay curious.

det.korean: 더 많이 배우고 호기심을 유지하기 위해 다양한 종류의 사람들과 시간을 보내라.
det.analysis: 원문: 'spend time with different kinds of people to learn more and stay curious.' 13단어 배열.
det.tip: spend time with = ~와 시간을 보내다. to learn more and stay curious = 더 배우고 호기심을 유지하기 위해.

questions.stem:
다음 우리말을 조건에 맞게 영작하시오.
"새로운 도전을 두려워하지 마세요. 용감해지세요!"
[조건] don't / afraid / challenges / brave 를 사용할 것
questions.wa: Don't be afraid of new challenges. Be brave!
accept: Don't be afraid of new challenges. Be brave!
don't be afraid of new challenges. be brave!
Don't be afraid of new challenges. Be brave

det.korean: 새로운 도전을 두려워하지 말고 용감해지라.
det.analysis: Don't be afraid of = ~을 두려워하지 마라. Be brave = 용감해져라.
det.tip: be afraid of = ~을 두려워하다. 부정 명령문: Don't + 동사원형.

questions.stem:
다음 우리말을 조건에 맞게 영작하시오.
"자기 계발은 완벽해짐에 관한 것이 아니다."
[조건] Self-improvement / not / about / perfect 를 사용할 것
questions.wa: Self-improvement is not about being perfect.
accept: Self-improvement is not about being perfect.
Self-improvement is not about being perfect
self-improvement is not about being perfect

det.korean: 자기 계발은 완벽해짐에 관한 것이 아니다.
det.analysis: Self-improvement is not about being perfect. about + -ing = ~에 관한.
det.tip: about + V-ing: ~에 관한. being perfect = 완벽해지는 것.
